dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET — LOWER CAVERN

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: There's a second distribution point at the east passage! There is no need to turn this one into a contest!

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: The east passage closed last night!

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I was not told that.*The worker gives him a look. He is young, with a bandaged thumb and a plain work vest that has been patched twice. Jex knows his face from shipping transactions but cannot find his name.*

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: We closed it after the heater failed. The door started sticking when the pipes contracted. Everybody who's queued for rations knows.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I had a verified distribution notice from four hours ago.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: Then you had the last person who knew about it four hours ago.

panelPlan: VEIL MARKET — LOWER CAVERN. A ration shutter jams halfway open. The people nearest it are pushed against the counter by the crowd behind them. Jex, attempting.
The shutter drops another finger's width. The nearest people begin pushing harder. A woman near the front raises a small child overhead so he can breathe. Jex.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *VEIL MARKET — LOWER CAVERN. A ration shutter jams halfway open. The people nearest it are pushed against the counter by the crowd behind them. Jex, attempting to get from one side to the other, loses his footing.*

*The shutter drops another finger's width. The nearest people begin pushing harder. A woman near the front raises a small child overhead so he can breathe. Jex tries to step between the counter and the crowd, slipping on spilled grain.*
sourceScene: SCENE 1 — THE SHUTTER (P01)

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Stop pushing! You're crushing the front row!

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You three, take two steps back and make a lane. Don't look at me; look at your neighbors. Help them move.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I assume nobody is putting that on the morning incident report.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: I already told dispatch your name. They asked whether you had a permit to operate the door.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: This is why I avoid public service.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: You can call me the man who got his grain yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Fair enough. I ought to find out why you only got it yesterday.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: Nobody tells the people who charge for the directions when the door's been welded shut.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Thank you. That was very nearly expensive.

panelPlan: Her voice carries because she sounds angry rather than official. She points to three adults near the edge.
The worker's laugh surprises both of them. He returns to the shutter. Jex remembers that he still does not know the man's name, and asks.
Two workers pull Jex free. One holds him against the wall until the crowd moves back.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Her voice carries because she sounds angry rather than official. She points to three adults near the edge.*
*A man hesitates, then starts pushing the crowd outward instead of forward. Others follow. It takes several ugly minutes before there's space to pull Jex clear.*
*The worker's laugh surprises both of them. He returns to the shutter. Jex remembers that he still does not know the man's name, and asks.*
*Two workers pull Jex free. One holds him against the wall until the crowd moves back.*
sourceScene: SCENE 1 — THE SHUTTER (P01)

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: For you, maybe.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You all right?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I have discovered how unpopular an out-of-date schedule can make a man.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: It would help if the schedules were less expensive.

panelPlan: She reaches behind the shutter to help release the jammed mechanism. Jex does not try to take credit for it.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

sourceScene: SCENE 1 — THE SHUTTER (P01)

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC FREEPORT

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: A hundred crates were promised. A hundred is what I've already committed to clinics and ration halls. I cannot distribute a hundred crates we do not have.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Where's the ship?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Outside the closed window. Nobody's flying an unverified reciprocal-field opening because we're impatient.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: People are getting impatient because they're hungry.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: And they'll be hungrier if we put the freighter through shear and spread it across the Rift.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: When can we verify another opening?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Jex has the live timing changes. I have the last public bulletin. They're not the same.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: Naturally.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Ask him.

panelPlan: AURIC FREEPORT. Wallace is moving three columns of expected supplies around an inventory board. Halev wants to authorize distribution; Naomi has just returned.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *AURIC FREEPORT. Wallace is moving three columns of expected supplies around an inventory board. Halev wants to authorize distribution; Naomi has just returned from Veil Market.*
sourceScene: SCENE 2 — ONE HUNDRED (P02–P03)

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I already have. He asked what we intended to pay.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Tell him we'll pay the pilots who use the information. I'll discuss his invoice when the food is here.

panelPlan: Halev stops writing.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Halev stops writing.*

summary: THE NAME THAT STILL OPENS DOORS (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO FLEET RESOURCE TRANSFER) — 1/5

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FLEET REVIEW ANNEX — COMMUNICATIONS BOOTH

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: I recognize the voice. I was hoping the caller identification was wrong.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: It's good to hear you too.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: Last time I heard that voice, somebody had put a cruiser on my calibration schedule without asking me.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: It was a small cruiser.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: It blocked my loading bay for a week.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Five days.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: Your people counted the days. My people counted the missed wages. We had different instruments.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I wanted to ask whether you could give Auric's maintenance office an independent assessment of their damaged sensor couplings. They'd contract you directly.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: I heard about the Tal Corvus arrivals. What makes you think I'm qualified to repair a shelter heating system?

panelPlan: FLEET REVIEW ANNEX — COMMUNICATIONS BOOTH. Venn has been permitted routine civilian correspondence during her restriction. On the other side of an ordinary.
Venn smiles. The surveyor does not entirely mean to be unfriendly.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *FLEET REVIEW ANNEX — COMMUNICATIONS BOOTH. Venn has been permitted routine civilian correspondence during her restriction. On the other side of an ordinary voice link sits a licensed surveyor who once maintained Fleet corridor instruments and now works privately. The surveyor, an older woman whose work jacket has paint on one cuff, has answered while repairing a thermal test stand. Her name is not entered into the public script record; her profession is.*
*Venn smiles. The surveyor does not entirely mean to be unfriendly.*
sourceScene: NEW SCENE V5-A — THE NAME THAT STILL OPENS DOORS (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO FLEET RESOURCE TRANSFER)

summary: THE NAME THAT STILL OPENS DOORS (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO FLEET RESOURCE TRANSFER) — 2/5

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I don't. I'm asking about the sensors that tell them whether a new corridor fitting is safe. A freighter can arrive with food, but the port has to know which equipment can receive it.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: So you need a survey, not a repair.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: Then why did you tell their office I could do both?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I used the wrong words.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: You used the words that would make the person hiring me think I'd solve both problems. That's not quite the same thing.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Fair criticism.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: You've never said that to me before. Are you in trouble?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: A certain amount.

panelPlan: Venn opens the draft she sent. She sees the phrasing. “Independent assessment and repair plan.” A phrase she'd thought safely general.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Venn opens the draft she sent. She sees the phrasing. “Independent assessment and repair plan.” A phrase she'd thought safely general.*
sourceScene: NEW SCENE V5-A — THE NAME THAT STILL OPENS DOORS (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO FLEET RESOURCE TRANSFER)

summary: THE NAME THAT STILL OPENS DOORS (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO FLEET RESOURCE TRANSFER) — 3/5

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: Good. I was starting to think the whole institution was immune.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: I'll talk to Auric. But I won't take a commission if they can't pay the crew. I'm not rich enough to replace the shipping bond, and I'm not taking a Fleet promise written by somebody who can't authorize it.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: That's fair.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: And I won't inspect a military screen while a civilian calls it a port survey. If there are guns involved, you tell me now.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: There are armed vessels in the region. I'm not asking you to evaluate their positions. If the job becomes one that needs military authorization, walk away.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: I'll decide that myself.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You should.

panelPlan: The surveyor sets down the fitting she's been holding.
Silence. The surveyor looks at the call header.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The surveyor sets down the fitting she's been holding.*
*Silence. The surveyor looks at the call header.*
sourceScene: NEW SCENE V5-A — THE NAME THAT STILL OPENS DOORS (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO FLEET RESOURCE TRANSFER)

summary: THE NAME THAT STILL OPENS DOORS (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO FLEET RESOURCE TRANSFER) — 4/5

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: You're not asking me to do it because of Kaldr, are you? Because of the grain ship?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I would have asked for help whether or not we'd been there.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: That's not an answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: No. I'm asking because we were there. I thought getting the passengers through was the end of my responsibility. It wasn't. And the people who have to live with the aftermath don't particularly want to hear me explain that.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: They've got a point.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Often.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: All right. Send me their public specification, not your Admiralty version of it. I'll quote against what Auric actually needs. If they reject the price, I want you to stay out of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Agreed.

panelPlan: Continue the conversation at the established location; let the speakers’ changing reactions carry it.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceScene: NEW SCENE V5-A — THE NAME THAT STILL OPENS DOORS (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO FLEET RESOURCE TRANSFER)

summary: THE NAME THAT STILL OPENS DOORS (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO FLEET RESOURCE TRANSFER) — 5/5

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: One thing. You remember telling the Chief at Kaldr that I'd always make room for Fleet?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I remember.

dialogueInline.speaker: SURVEYOR
dialogueInline.text: I didn't make room for Fleet. I made room for the wounded people you were carrying. There's a difference. It would be pleasant if you remembered it this time.

panelPlan: The call ends. Venn removes the loose reference to “repair plan” from the request and sends a corrected public specification to Auric. The surveyor may accept.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: JEX'S PRIVATE VAULT

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You're not selling a route. You're selling the difference between a safe crossing and a collision with the boundary.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I prefer to think I'm selling the work of people who measure that difference.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: And the ship whose food is sitting on the wrong side of it?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: They could have bought the update.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Nobody told them the old one was wrong.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: If I open the current clock, Billie can read it. Pike can read it. Every fool with a gun and a receiver can read it.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Yes.

panelPlan: JEX'S PRIVATE VAULT. Three different live opening corrections are visible on a simple instrument record. Jex has kept the verified updates to sell. Naomi.
He opens his mouth, then closes it. There's no defense that doesn't sound like a price.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *JEX'S PRIVATE VAULT. Three different live opening corrections are visible on a simple instrument record. Jex has kept the verified updates to sell. Naomi recognizes one shift she has already seen in the field.*
*He opens his mouth, then closes it. There's no defense that doesn't sound like a price.*
sourceScene: SCENE 3 — WHAT A CLOCK COSTS (P04–P05)

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: You've become an unhelpful conversationalist.*Naomi does not answer immediately. She is studying the three corrections and the intervals between them. A faint discrepancy has the look of an instrument carried outside its calibration range. She circles one observation.*

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Who supplied this one?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: An independent survey crew. Their ship is competent, their debt is modest, and I believe their captain is only lying to one spouse at the moment.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You trust it?

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I trust it enough to put my name on the bulletin. That's a considerably more expensive form of trust than the one I ordinarily sell.

panelPlan: Continue the conversation at the established location; let the speakers’ changing reactions carry it.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceScene: SCENE 3 — WHAT A CLOCK COSTS (P04–P05)

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: There'll be days when the correction is wrong. If the field changes faster than they report it, people will blame you.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: People already blame me for things I haven't done. At least this time I'll have the satisfaction of knowing I did something.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You can keep the transaction record. We aren't asking you to burn every useful thing you've built.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I don't think you understand what happens when a broker gives up being the only man who knows where the road goes.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: He may have to start being useful in another way.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You know what I think. I came to see what you think when you can't hide behind a price.

panelPlan: He opens the private subscriber list. Pilots who used to pay for early corrections now receive the same public update as crews who could never afford them..
Jex confirms. One subscriber immediately messages to complain that the secret he bought is no longer secret. Jex starts to type an answer, deletes.
Jex transfers the verified current updates to a public bulletin, including corrections as they arrive.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Keep your pilots checking measurements. If the field changes, this paper will become a lie before I've finished publishing it.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Good. Put that on the notice too.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: It's remarkable how much more you ask when I'm giving things away.

panelPlan: The bulletin becomes available to the civilian freighter. Elsewhere, Ashfang receives the same timing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: ASHFANG MARAUDER

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Enough to reach the next staging point. Not enough to fight there and come back.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Then we don't fight there.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: A hundred crates on a Verge relief freighter. We've got their crossing time.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: That's food for somebody.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: So are the stores we don't have. You told Trade to keep their tankers.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: We take the supply rack. Quick and out. Keep the weapons off the cabins.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: We're losing the rack! Stop firing! This is food!

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We didn't get any of it.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I can see that.

panelPlan: ASHFANG MARAUDER. The Triarch has cut Billie's fuel deliveries because she refused to burn independent Shard fields. Her officer has been stretching the.
In the Rift, Ashfang fires first. The aft rack tears loose. Twenty-eight of the hundred promised crates are destroyed, not captured. The freighter.
Billie's officer watches a cloud of ruined cargo move away from the ship.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *ASHFANG MARAUDER. The Triarch has cut Billie's fuel deliveries because she refused to burn independent Shard fields. Her officer has been stretching the remaining stores and no longer bothers to pretend the figures are adequate.*
*Billie stares at the timing bulletin Jex opened. She chooses an interdiction she knows Abby would reject.*
*In the Rift, Ashfang fires first. The aft rack tears loose. Twenty-eight of the hundred promised crates are destroyed, not captured. The freighter struggles to maintain course.*
*Billie's officer watches a cloud of ruined cargo move away from the ship.*
sourceScene: SCENE 4 — ASHFANG HAS NO FUEL (P06–P10)

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: The rest could still feed us if we catch the freighter.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Billie, don't make me explain the people inside that hull to you.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Move. We need the remaining freight.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: So do the people it belongs to.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You haven't missed a meal yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: My crew has. I can still tell the difference between a meal and somebody else's supper.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Captain, her port section is barely holding together.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: I know. She put it right where I'd have to hit it.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We can turn her.

panelPlan: Gravefire enters on its already damaged port side. Tess places its heat-weakened radiator between Ashfang and the freighter.
Gravefire's cooling warning climbs. Tess is not bluffing about what one more shot would do.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

*Gravefire's cooling warning climbs. Tess is not bluffing about what one more shot would do.*

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: You can stop suggesting I shoot Tess. Break off.*The officer obeys. Ashfang rolls away and the freighter moves toward its escort, still venting debris from the destroyed rack. For a while Billie listens to the ship rather than the crew. A bearing sounds wrong after the turn. She asks for engineering.*

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEERING
dialogueInline.text: Same starboard coupling. It's been running hot since Black Drift. We can't repair it with what we've got.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: And the fuel?

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEERING
dialogueInline.text: Enough to get home if you don't change your mind about leaving.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We could ask the captain to transfer a few medical cases. Gravefire would escort them. Tess might agree.

panelPlan: She looks at the retreating freighter. Tess has not opened another channel. The absence is worse than an argument.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *She looks at the retreating freighter. Tess has not opened another channel. The absence is worse than an argument.*

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: After we shot twenty-eight crates into space? Would you agree if you were her?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: Then don't make me ask her for something I haven't earned.

panelPlan: The officer leaves to tell the galley the expected food hasn't arrived. Billie can hear the conversation from her station; the cook asks whether to cut the.
Ashfang withdraws with no supplies, a damaged reputation, and less fuel than before.

summary: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE CLOCK (P11–P12) — 1/2

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: VEIL MARKET SERVICE CAVERN

dialogueInline.speaker: LOADER
dialogueInline.text: Twenty-eight.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I heard.

dialogueInline.speaker: LOADER
dialogueInline.text: You heard someone say a number. You didn't open the broken crates to find out what was inside.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Was there anything salvageable?

dialogueInline.speaker: LOADER
dialogueInline.text: You could make soup out of the labels.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I'll send a recovery crew.

dialogueInline.speaker: LOADER
dialogueInline.text: With what? The clock you opened told every ship where we were. Ashfang read it as well as anybody.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: So did the freighter. So did the escorts who came to help.

dialogueInline.speaker: LOADER
dialogueInline.text: You always have another side to it.

panelPlan: VEIL MARKET SERVICE CAVERN. Naomi follows a worker's chalk arrow toward a ration door that is actually open, ignoring an older official marker. A loader.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

summary: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE CLOCK (P11–P12) — 2/2

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Usually three. That's how I make a living.

dialogueInline.speaker: LOADER
dialogueInline.text: I had a cart, Jex. They had guns. You're welcome to find the third side.

dialogueInline.speaker: LOADER
dialogueInline.text: My sister gets her allotment every fourth crossing. She asks me for an extra bag of grain. I've spent a month telling her no. Now I get to explain why we lost twenty-eight bags' worth before anyone got to eat them.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I didn't tell Billie to attack.

dialogueInline.speaker: LOADER
dialogueInline.text: I know. If I thought you had, we wouldn't be talking.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Then why ask me to close the clock?

dialogueInline.speaker: LOADER
dialogueInline.text: I didn't ask you. Don't close it. My sister's still waiting. But if you've got information about who's coming to take her grain next time, I wouldn't mind hearing it before the shooting starts.

Jex looks at the bulletin. He continues posting corrections. Tali's private token stays out of public view.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: I can authorize the inspection. I cannot authorize the equipment the inspector hasn't identified yet. Your surveyor seems disappointed by that.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: She's usually disappointed when people ask her to certify something they've already decided to buy.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Then she and I may get on very well. She wants two independent readings and a local escort. That's doable. She wants permission to keep the raw recordings for her insurance. That's not.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Why not?

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Because the recordings show where we berth damaged ships and how long we leave the outer dock exposed. The equipment might be civilian; the information can still put people in danger.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: She needs enough to document her calculation. Could she keep anonymized equipment readings and have Auric retain the positions?

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: That's exactly what my clerk suggested before you called.

dialogueInline.speaker: CLERK
dialogueInline.text: I suggested it more politely.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: She did. I was in a less receptive mood then.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I'm relieved to have arrived during your receptive one.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Don't become accustomed to it. There's another problem. The survey team would need two hours of warmth and a clear working bay. Two hours we currently use to process emergency arrivals. I can move them, but the people in that bay have already moved twice.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I could ask Fleet to provide a temporary working platform.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Could you?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: I'm glad we've dispensed with that in under a sentence.

dialogueInline.speaker: CLERK
dialogueInline.text: If the survey happens after the incoming relief freight clears, we only need one bay for one hour. It costs us a shift of inspection backlog, not sleeping space.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Assuming the freight clears. It was attacked this morning. Our promised hundred crates are now seventy-two.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I saw the preliminary report.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Did you see what the missing twenty-eight means? They were supposed to restock two clinics. A captain chose to shoot off an equipment rack, and the people who ordered her food deliveries stopped will still eat before we do.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I don't have an answer that makes it smaller.

panelPlan: The clerk runs the numbers. A small adjustment appears on her screen.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Good. I'm becoming tired of people with excellent answers and no crates.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Then don't schedule the survey yet. If the cargo berth and your crews are free after the next run, you can bring her in. If not, defer it. She can prepare from the redacted specifications. Neither I nor the surveyor gets to decide whether that hour is worth more than your arrivals work.

dialogueInline.speaker: CLERK
dialogueInline.text: That means we can obtain a price for the test without committing the shift.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: I see why Commodore Venn became popular with her engineers. She can still be persuaded to accept the obvious after several minutes.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I was considerably worse when I had a ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: That's what Naomi tells me.

panelPlan: Venn thinks for a moment. She chooses not to invoke a colleague.
The clerk smiles despite an exhausted face. Sera notices and softens.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: I'll authorize a conditional quotation, subject to local control of the evidence. If this works, it helps us certify equipment. If it fails, we will have spent an hour discovering an old sensor is old. Please don't have Fleet issue a celebration for either outcome.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I won't.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: And Commodore? The surveyor is now dealing with my office. You don't need to remain in the middle of every message.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Understood.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THUNDERBREAK — COMMAND

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Admiralty approved a defensive screen for this freight escort. No offensive release.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: That's more than I expected.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: I'd celebrate, but the next line says we can't interfere with Shard command decisions.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: We weren't planning to.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Banks is holding that line with a damaged port radiator.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I can see it. She's keeping her hot side away from the freighter and doing our job with half a cooling circuit.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire still shows Shard hostile.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Keep the designation. Give her civilian overlap and cover her exposed side.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: We could ask for confirmation through the Admiralty chain. If the screen is misinterpreted as an alliance, the report comes back to you.

panelPlan: THUNDERBREAK — COMMAND. The cruiser has orders to offer a limited defensive screen for the next freight escort. Deka sits in the captain's station; the port.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: It probably will. We can wait for a better report or we can cover a real ship. How long until the freighter reaches the dangerous part?

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Eleven minutes.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Then we should probably spend ten of them doing something useful.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire, Thunderbreak. We can hold overlap along your exposed port approach. Your crossing order stays yours.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS (COMMS)
dialogueInline.text: That's reassuring. I'm sure the next Admiralty letter will be equally friendly.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: I wouldn't make plans around it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Keep the shield on the freight, then. I can take care of my ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: That's why I'm offering it.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: If you cut her off, Billie will say you've left Ashfang blind.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: She wasn't blind when she fired at the relief freighter. She knew exactly what was on it.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: She also knew the crew's fuel allocation had been cut. Her people are hungry.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: So are the people who needed those crates.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: You've known her longer than most of us have been alive. Are you sure you want this recorded as a sanction?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I remember the first time she lent me an engine part without asking what she was getting back. I also remember the last time she did it. It wasn't all that long ago.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Then call her.

panelPlan: Abby walks to the observation pane. From here the Shard ships are still a working fleet of independent captains, not an army she can order home.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Abby walks to the observation pane. From here the Shard ships are still a working fleet of independent captains, not an army she can order home.*
sourceScene: SCENE 6 — WHAT THE CAPTAINS CAN WITHHOLD (P13–P14)

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: If I call, she'll talk me into remembering everything except what happened to that freighter. I'm not ready for that conversation.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: She'll say you chose Fleet over her.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I chose not to give her the timing of the next civilian shipment. That should be a distinction she'd understand.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: She can fly wherever she chooses. She still commands Ashfang. I am not taking her ship, or the people who trust her. I'm withholding something that depends on trusting her myself.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Will you tell her?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Yes. Not through a notice she can show her crew and make a martyr out of. I'll tell her when she answers my call.

panelPlan: She signs the restriction. The officer hesitates.
The call is placed. It rings. Abby sits waiting, but Billie does not answer. The unanswered call stays in the log. That unanswered call is an injury of its own.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC — FREIGHT HALL

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: Don't write 'hundred received' because the manifest still says a hundred. We have seventy-two on the dock.

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: I know how to count crates.

dialogueInline.speaker: SERA
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't speaking to your arithmetic. I was speaking to the very persuasive way people edit their own expectations.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: How much do we cut each allotment?

dialogueInline.speaker: WALLACE
dialogueInline.text: The clinics get their original share. Everyone else gets less. The people who already had very little get less as well.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Put the numbers where they can see them.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: We can come back tomorrow, can't we?

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: They didn't say we'd have more tomorrow.

panelPlan: Auric freight hall. The ship arrives with seventy-two crates. Sera insists the board keep the missing twenty-eight visible as a debt the station cannot fulfill.
A family at the distribution bay voluntarily breaks a small allotment to share with a resident whose household missed registration. The boy from Luminara.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: No. I suppose they didn't.*His mother reaches for the bag, then stops. The boy had offered their food without permission and knows it. He waits for the reprimand. It doesn't come.*

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: How much did you give away?

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: Not everything. I kept the part you said was for breakfast.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: That's considerate of you. I'm not sure the breakfast you saved is enough for breakfast.

dialogueInline.speaker: BOY
dialogueInline.text: There are two of us. We can share.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: It's broth. Not much of it. My neighbor had some vegetables and made a pot.

dialogueInline.speaker: MOTHER
dialogueInline.text: You needn't repay us.

dialogueInline.speaker: RESIDENT
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't repaying you. I was hoping you knew where to find another cup.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FLEET REVIEW ANNEX — VISITING ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You've been busy.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I've been confined to two rooms for weeks. The alternative was to become very good at cards.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Kerr. An independent surveyor. Auric's elected officials. One retired civilian contractor who used to have Fleet work. Did you think no one would notice?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I expected you to notice. I wasn't certain you'd take the time to visit.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You're making private approaches to people responsible for a region in which Fleet vessels are currently engaged. Your tribunal finding remains in force.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I have issued no orders. Nobody has used Fleet authority on my request. The contractor can walk away, and Auric decides whether to employ her.

panelPlan: FLEET REVIEW ANNEX — VISITING ROOM. Dominion has come without an audience or ceremonial escort. A security officer remains outside the door. He places a list.

summary: A PRIVATE CHAIN OF COMMAND (AFTER SOURCE P17; BEFORE THE SECOND RELIEF CONVOY) — 2/5

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: And when someone says yes because your name is Ella Venn rather than because the work is sound?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Then I've built a chain of command I can pretend isn't one.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You understand why that concerns me.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I do.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Yet you continue.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Because Auric needs equipment and reliable measurements. The public route exists. The cargo losses exist. I can leave the institution's private arguments to you and still ask a licensed person whether she wants a job.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You once commanded a cruiser. Now you sound like a hiring agent.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I've had a few difficult conversations about the difference.

panelPlan: That lands. Venn doesn't conceal it.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

summary: A PRIVATE CHAIN OF COMMAND (AFTER SOURCE P17; BEFORE THE SECOND RELIEF CONVOY) — 3/5

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: If what you wanted was a hearing about refugee supplies, you could submit one. Instead you've chosen to cultivate the people who will testify when Fleet asks for continued access.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Some of them already dislike me. I find that reassuring.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Don't confuse being disliked with being harmless.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Your successor covered a Shard ship classified as hostile. Under restricted defensive orders. We are reviewing the judgment.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I know what Deka did. I don't know why she judged it necessary. You should ask her.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You haven't spoken to her?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: No. I won't make my reputation an extra officer on her bridge.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Your restraint is new.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: My circumstances are new. I'd like to think I'm learning from them.

panelPlan: Dominion slides a second page toward her. It is a disciplinary accounting of *Thunderbreak*'s defensive support for *Gravefire*, recorded under Deka's command.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

summary: A PRIVATE CHAIN OF COMMAND (AFTER SOURCE P17; BEFORE THE SECOND RELIEF CONVOY) — 4/5

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: I won't promise to forgive her for making a defensible choice. Or condemn her for one. Her tasking has limits, whether or not you agree with them.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Then evaluate the limits. Not me.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: I'm placing your external technical correspondence under declared review. You may send public specifications and legal requests. Not operational positions, no tasking, no informal requests to Fleet personnel. Kerr will receive the record. If you cross that line, you'll lose even this room.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You're giving me a boundary instead of silence.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: I'm giving myself a reason to stop this before people begin taking orders from an officer who has been removed from command.

panelPlan: Dominion closes the file. The room holds an uncomfortable truce.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Those are the same boundary, Admiral. We disagree about what it's for.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: I always thought taking *Thunderbreak* from you would mean you'd have fewer opportunities to cause trouble.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: So did I.

panelPlan: Dominion stands.
He goes. Venn spends the rest of the evening preparing a written list of her civilian contacts and exactly what each has been asked to do. Several entries.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THE NEXT RELIEF CONVOY — APPROACH

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: Your approach looks too shallow. I'm going to overshoot the mark.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You're going to overshoot if you keep staring at the wrong instrument. Look at the physical reference off your port side.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER PILOT
dialogueInline.text: That's not the published course.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: It is the course that exists right now. You can argue with me after you're docked. I like a captive audience.

dialogueInline.speaker: WOMAN
dialogueInline.text: This one works. Don't trust yesterday's arrow.

sourceActionBeats: *The next relief convoy approaches. Naomi leads with Sunlash, Tess brings Gravefire despite the limitation of its damaged cooling system, and a Fleet escort holds to the agreed defensive role.*

*The ship corrects. At Veil Market, civilians update another chalk route to a working distribution door. The official notice is already behind events. A woman checks the opening herself before telling anyone else to follow.*
*No one confuses the guidance with a permanent solution. The food arrives and the people carry it home.*

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: We can seize the board.

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: And the copies?

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: There are too many to trace.

dialogueInline.speaker: FEAR MASK
dialogueInline.text: Then stop looking for boards. Find the people who carry them. They can be frightened, bribed, or made to doubt what they've seen.
